summary: # CLO Skills Workshop - Production of Reflective Strips ## Introduction In this workshop, we will explore the process of creating a backlight strip in Clover. Follow these steps to effectively produce reflective strips using various tools and settings. ## Adding a Name Line First, add a name line to the place where the backlight strip needs to be integrated. 1. Modify the name line type to "text." 2. You can view the name line text here. ## Creating Backlight Strip Text in Photoshop Next, make a backlight strip text in Photoshop (PS). 1. Set the size of the text to **100x200 pixels.** 2. Set the resolution to **300 DPI.** ### Sourcing Texture For the texture, you can either find images or directly scan the material to create a texture. 1. Process the interface of the texture. 2. After processing, save the texture file. ## Adding Texture to the Backlight Strip Once you have saved the texture, proceed with the following steps: 1. Add the texture to the name line. 2. Set the strength of the backlight strip to **20.** 3. Use this setup to create a backlight strip. ## Material and Surface Adjustments Next, configure the material settings: 1. Set the material to **metal.** 2. Adjust the roughness of the surface to **40.** 3. Set the strength of the backlight to **100.** 4. Adjust the metal density to **80.** ### Adjusting Thickness Now, focus on the thickness settings: 1. Set the thickness of the name line to **5 mm.** 2. Set the thickness of the line to **1 cm.** 3. This defines the width of the backlight strip you require. ## Adding Backlight Strips to Curves To add backlight strips to a curve, follow these steps: 1. Use the free name line to create a whole circle of name lines. 2. Note that the previous settings may cause incompatibility in the position and thickness of the backlight strip. ### Copying Name Lines 1. Copy a name line in the canvas window. 2. Change this name line to the original name line. 3. Open the **Attribute Editor**. ### Adjusting Name Line Attributes In the Attribute Editor, make the following adjustments: 1. Set the gap of the name line to **1.5 mm.** 2. Adjust the length of the line to **1 mm.** 3. Set the thickness of the line to **0.30 mm.** 4. Finally, adjust the thickness of the line to **3 mm.** These adjustments ensure that the position and size are compatible with the curve line. ## Smoothing the Texture If you notice creases in the texture of the line, use the edit line tool: 1. Select the line. 2. Open the **Curve and Smooth** option in the Attribute Editor. 3. This will smooth out the backlight strip, eliminating any creases. ### Final Adjustments 1. If there's a small crease at the end of the line, add another line to cover it. 2. Ensure to turn over this new line as well. 3. You should see that the whole edge is now smooth. ## Creating New Lines Finally, to create a new line: 1. Click to turn over. 2. Add another line to the curve. 3. The line should now appear smooth. ## Conclusion By following these detailed steps, you can successfully create and adjust backlight strips within Clover, ensuring high-quality, reflective outputs tailored to your needs.
